evidence.role: particle-property and nuclear-composition demand inspiration; original wording

hints: Separate the tiny central region from the surrounding region.
For each particle, give both location and charge.

walkthrough.text: Identify the nucleus as the central region.
Place positive protons and neutrons with no net charge in the nucleus.
Place negatively charged electrons orbiting outside the nucleus.

ai_rubric.observable: States that protons are positively charged and are in the nucleus
States that neutrons have no net charge and are in the nucleus
States that negatively charged electrons orbit outside the nucleus

evidence.role: straight-path inference demand inspiration; original options

hints: Ask what most particles fail to meet.
Distinguish atomic volume from atomic mass.

walkthrough.text: Most alpha particles cross the foil without a strong interaction.
Therefore most of each atom contains no concentrated matter capable of strongly deflecting them.
Most of the atom is empty space, so select A.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects A, inferring that most of the atom is empty space

evidence.role: large-angle inference demand inspiration; original options

hints: The alpha particle has positive charge.
A large deflection needs a strong force during close approach.

walkthrough.text: A positive alpha particle is repelled only by positive charge.
A large deflection requires a strong interaction with concentrated charge.
The cause is a small region of concentrated positive charge, so select B.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B, identifying a small region of concentrated positive charge

evidence.role: particle-property demand inspiration; original row choices

hints: Recall which two particles form the nucleus.
Electrons occupy the region outside the nucleus.

walkthrough.text: Protons and neutrons are nucleons located in the nucleus.
Electrons orbit outside the nucleus.
Only row C gives both locations correctly.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects C, placing protons and neutrons in the nucleus and electrons outside

evidence.role: paired observation-to-inference demand inspiration; original detector diagram

hints: Treat the common and rare paths as separate observations.
For the rare path, connect positive alpha charge, frequency and deflection size to three different properties.

walkthrough.text: Use group P to infer how much atomic volume contains concentrated matter.
Use repulsion in group R to infer the sign of nuclear charge.
Use the rarity of R for nuclear size and the size of its deflection for concentration of mass.

hints: Most tracks show no strong encounter.

walkthrough.text: Group P contains most of the recorded tracks.
Those particles pass through with little or no deflection.
Therefore most atomic volume is empty space.

ai_rubric.observable: Infers from the many straight paths that most of the atom is empty space

hints: A positive alpha particle is repelled by positive charge.
Use rarity for size and the large direction change for concentration of mass.

walkthrough.text: The positive alpha particle is strongly repelled, so the nucleus is positive.
Only one representative path shows this close encounter, so the nucleus occupies a very small volume.
The large change of motion supports that nearly all atomic mass is concentrated in the nucleus.

ai_rubric.observable: Infers that the nucleus is positively charged from strong repulsion of a positive alpha particle
Infers from the rarity of the large deflection that the nucleus is very small
Infers from the large deflection that nearly all atomic mass is concentrated in the nucleus

evidence.role: nuclear-model property and evidence reasoning inspiration; original flawed model

hints: Separate correct particle locations from incorrect scale.
Predict what would happen if concentrated matter filled half the atom.

walkthrough.text: Credit the placement of protons and neutrons in the nucleus and electrons outside.
Recall that most alpha particles cross with little or no deflection.
A nucleus filling half the atom would cause frequent strong encounters, contradicting the result, so the nucleus must be very small.

hints: Look only at which particles are inside and outside.

walkthrough.text: The model places both protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
It places electrons outside the nucleus.
These are the two accepted features.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies that protons and neutrons are in the nucleus
Identifies that electrons are outside the nucleus

hints: Compare the predicted collision frequency with the observed frequency.

walkthrough.text: Most alpha particles are observed to pass straight through the foil.
A nucleus occupying half the atomic volume would be encountered often and would produce many deflections.
The prediction contradicts the observation, so the nucleus must occupy a very small volume.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the observation that most alpha particles pass through with little or no deflection
Explains that the observation requires the nucleus to occupy a very small fraction of atomic volume

evidence.role: closest-approach and particle-property demand inspiration; original diagram

hints: Rank the paths by closest approach to the centre.
Then connect like-charge repulsion to the complete nuclear model.

walkthrough.text: Compare X, Y and Z by their distance of closest approach to the tiny centre.
Use the positive charges of alpha particle and nucleus to explain repulsion.
Finish by placing protons and neutrons at the centre and electrons outside.

hints: Closer approach means stronger repulsion.

walkthrough.text: X stays far from the nucleus, so it has little or no deflection.
Y passes closer and has a moderate deflection.
Z approaches closest and therefore has the largest deflection, possibly turning back.

ai_rubric.observable: Predicts little or no deflection for X and a greater deflection for Y
Predicts the largest deflection for Z because it approaches closest to the nucleus

hints: Name both charge signs before stating the interaction.

walkthrough.text: The alpha particle carries positive charge.
The nucleus also carries positive charge because it contains protons.
Like charges repel, so Z is pushed away rather than attracted.

ai_rubric.observable: States that both the alpha particle and the nucleus are positively charged
Explains that like charges repel, causing Z to deflect away from the nucleus

hints: Group the two nucleons together, then place electrons.

walkthrough.text: Put protons and neutrons together in the tiny central nucleus.
Put electrons on orbits outside the nucleus in the surrounding atomic region.

ai_rubric.observable: Places protons and neutrons in the central nucleus
Places electrons orbiting outside the nucleus
